title: unified-rollouts: enhanced canary + shadow + A/B autorollback enhancements
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: reduce rollout churn and false positive rollbacks while enabling richer deployment patterns (canary + A/B + shadow) and better observability for automated rollback decisions. This PR implements multi-stage canary + A/B weighting with shadow traffic metric matching, composite metric quorum evaluation, and stability guards to avoid flapping. Summary of changes: - Autorollback engine: add composite metric evaluator, quorum-based decisioning, and metric window alignment for shadow traffic. - Canary controller: support multi-stage progressive canaries with configurable staging windows and hold times. - A/B routing: add dynamic traffic weighting and fallback policies for immediate rollback or gradual drain. - Shadow probing: introduce staged probing + quarantine when anomalies detected on shadow-only routes. - Observability: new rollout-level metrics, traces, and dashboard panels; improve rollback reason logging for post-mortems. - Tests: unit + integration + e2e canary/shadow flows and stability guards. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: ENG-4312 (linked) - [x] Implementation of composite metric + quorum - [x] Backwards compatible config parsing for existing rollout specs - [x] E2E tests for canary -> A/B -> shadow transitions - [x] Add telemetry and dashboard changes - [x] Load-tested against synthetic production traffic in perf-canary Summary of behavioral changes: - Autorollback now evaluates a composite of metrics (latency P95, error rate, model output-regression score) and requires a quorum of breached metrics before triggering automatic rollback. This reduces single-metric false positives. - Shadow traffic metrics are aligned to production routes by time-window and request-tag matching so regressions in shadowed models are comparable to live traffic. - A/B experiments support weighted rollouts with automated fallback to 0% for failing variants while allowing other variants to continue. - Staged probing will quarantine suspect variants and isolate them from broader rollouts until manual review/clearance. Why this is safe: defaults are conservative (short probe exposures, small initial canary percentages, require quorum and sustained breach over multiple windows). Operators can opt into aggressive policies via rollout policy flags. Related: ENG-4450 (e2e stability guards), SUP-8792 (customer incident that motivated metric-quorum behavior).

review_conversation: Diego Ramirez: Left a high-level comment asking for clarity on how quorum is computed across heterogeneous metrics. Requested a unit test that covers latency+error+score combination.

Maya Chen: Reply: added test_quorum_logic.py and expanded docstring in engine.py explaining normalization and weighted aggregation. The quorum requires at least 2/3 metrics breached by default (configurable).
Priya Nair: Requested that shadow metric windowing align with production route timestamps to avoid time-shifted comparisons. Noted potential edge-case for batched ingestion.
Maya Chen: Reply: adjusted shadow/prober to tag shadow requests with production route timestamps and added a dedupe step for batched requests. Added explanation in unified-rollouts.md.
Evan Zhou: Verified performance impact: perf-canary shows <2% p50 token latency regression at 95th percentile load. Approved after e2e passes.

release_notes:
- Introduce composite-metric quorum-based autorollback to reduce false positives.
- Multi-stage canary support with configurable staging windows and hold times.
- A/B weighted rollouts with automated fallback for failing variants.
- Staged shadow probing and quarantine flow for safer model onboarding.
- New rollout-level telemetry and dashboarding for rollback reasons and composite metrics.
safety_guards: Defaults are conservative: small initial canaries (1-5%), short probe exposures, require quorum (2/3) sustained across multiple windows before autorollback triggers. Manual override and audit logs available.
notes: This change is primarily additive and backwards compatible. Existing rollout specs will continue to work; new fields are optional. Operator docs updated with migration examples and troubleshooting steps.
